Nov 8 : Two-time major winner Jon Rahm sealed a triumphant return to the DP World Tour on Sunday, winning the Abu Dhabi Championship a month after leaving LIV Golf. It was the former world number one's first tournament since he left the breakaway circuit, and the Spaniard hit a five-under 67 in Sunday's fourth round to finish 23-under, earning his 11th title on the DP World Tour. Tyrrell Hatton took second place, finishing two strokes behind Rahm, while Rory McIlroy was third. "It means a lot. Still almost not letting myself believe it. It's been quite a while since I've played good in a DP World Tour event," said Rahm, who had joined LIV Golf in 2023.

"In my last showing, if you don't count the withdrawals, I think I finished last. So, from last to first is a pretty good feeling." Rahm rose to the top of the leaderboard after the second round, sharing the position with Hatton and Francesco Laporta despite hitting three bogeys on the day. He claimed a solo lead on Saturday with an eagle and five birdies, finishing a stroke ahead of Laporta. The 31-year-old, who welcomed his fourth child with wife Kelley Cahill last month, shook off a bogey on the third hole to solidify his lead with six birdies in the final round. "After everything that's gone on and some poor play and some battles, mentally, with a lot of the noise, to come back out after a little bit of rest and having a new addition to the family, it's quite special," Rahm added. "I only wish they were here to celebrate with me."

Source: Reuters

Nov 8 : Anthropic has struck a deal worth about $3.4 billion to secure gas-fired power generators for data centers, the Financial Times reported on Sunday. The AI startup bought commitments for 1.7 gigawatts of heavy-duty generators in late September from OnePWR Solutions, a San Antonio, Texas-based equipment supplier, the report said. Anthropic did not acquire OnePWR itself, and none of the supplier's employees transferred to the AI startup, but the deal included engineering and construction capabilities needed to install the generators, the report added, citing a person familiar with the matter.  Reuters could not immediately verify the report and Anthropic and OnePWR did not respond to requests for comment. Strong demand for Anthropic's Claude family of AI models has prompted the company to secure additional computing and power capacity. Reuters reported in September that Anthropic expects to spend more than $500 billion over the next 10 years building AI infrastructure.

Source: Reuters

SYDNEY, Nov 8 : Reece Walsh scored a hat-trick as reigning champions Australia caught fire on a chilly evening to beat Samoa 44-12 and reach the Rugby League World Cup final for the 13th time on Sunday.  The tournament hosts ran in eight tries to secure a trip to Brisbane next Sunday for the title decider against New Zealand, who beat Tonga 34-10 in the other semi-final at Lang Park on Saturday. The 12-times world champions had been under fire for limp performances in the group stage but finally found their groove in this rematch of the 2022 final. "There was a lot of emotion at the start of the game... that’s the pressure of these big matches that you need to go out and have your best performance. I thought we did that tonight," said Australian captain Isaah Yeo.

"The conditions were tough. It was sort of on-and-off-again rain. The wind was sort of annoying for both sides, I reckon... but it just sort of just let our X-factor players shine." Halfback Tom Dearden, second row Jacob Preston, winger Tom Trbojevic, Walsh and centre Bradman Best all scored tries to give Australia a 26-2 halftime lead. Samoa had the most vocal support in the sellout crowd of 41,529 at Sydney Football Stadium but their talented team were only able to give them an early Stephen Crichton penalty to cheer before the break. Crichton finally got them over the try line early in the second half off a Walsh error but the Kangaroos fullback scored his second try three minutes later. Centre Izack Tago had the Samoan flags flying again when he crossed in the corner on the hour mark but Walsh soon had his hat-trick to put Australia 38-12 ahead. Winger Jack Bostock crossed for Australia's eighth try in a last 10 minutes of action punctuated by scuffles, with Cameron Munster kicking his sixth conversion to round out the scoring.

Nov 8 : Japan Football Association Honorary President Kozo Tashima said governance was FIFA's biggest problem as he outlined his platform for next year's presidential election, while rating his chances of unseating incumbent Gianni Infantino at 20 per cent to 30 per cent. Tashima announced on Thursday that he intended to run in the March election, becoming the first Japanese candidate to seek world football's top job. The 68-year-old former Japan international has served on the FIFA Council since 2015 and became JFA president the following year before being succeeded by Tsuneyasu Miyamoto in 2024. "I've received many messages saying, 'Thank you for speaking out'...," Tashima told Japanese daily Sports Nippon in an interview published on Sunday.

"I've been contacted by presidents and international department officials from eight countries, including some outside Asia. "While I haven't received any formal endorsements yet, I'm getting a positive response. Since time is short and I don't want to be held up by incomplete paperwork, I want to secure support from at least six associations." Tashima requires nominations from five national associations, a prerequisite for standing in the election. Candidates have until November 18 to submit nominations for the election, in which Infantino is seeking a fourth term as head of world soccer's governing body. Infantino came under scrutiny in July after an unsuccessful attempt to bring private investors into a new FIFA commercial entity holding rights linked to competitions including the World Cup. Despite the criticism, Infantino's candidacy received a significant boost in October when the head of Asian football publicly endorsed him, while support from several FIFA confederations has left him well placed among the organisation's 211 member associations. "I'll keep what's good and change what's bad...," Tashima added. "The biggest problem, however, remains governance... "Selflessness is my motto... At this stage, I think my chances of winning are about 20 per cent to 30 per cent, but as the campaign progresses, I want to raise my confidence to 40 per cent or 50 per cent. I truly want to change FIFA." Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega was the first candidate to publicly declare his intention to challenge fellow Swiss Infantino last month.

Source: Reuters

Nov 8 : Luca Van Assche fell short in his bid to become the first French winner of the Paris Masters since 2008, but he will take plenty of positives from a strong run which ended in a semi-final defeat by world number four Ben Shelton. Van Assche, ranked 47th in the world, pushed Shelton hard and took the first set in Saturday's semi-final, before eventually losing 5-7 6-3 6-4 to the American in front of home fans. "It is true that this week is very important for me because I have a lot of high-level matches under my belt in a row. I played Shelton, who is number four in the world," the 22-year-old told reporters after his defeat. "That showed everything that I could do well, where I have some room for progress. This will help me to have more self-confidence, I know now that I can reach a semi-final.

Van Assche's run in Paris means he will rise to a career-high ranking of 34th in the world when the latest rankings are published on Monday. Asked if he was aiming to be among the seeded players at next year's Australian Open in January, he said: "I don't think I'm going to think along those lines. But above all, I will try to remain focused on my game, on learning new skills, on progressing, and then the ranking will follow." Nov 8 : Usman Khawaja on Sunday denied that he had "thrown anyone under the bus", a day after an excerpt from the former Australian cricketer's autobiography claimed the entire team had been aware of ball-tampering during a 2018 tour of South Africa. The scandal, dubbed "Sandpapergate" over Australia's scuffing of the ball with sandpaper in the March 2018 test in Cape Town, sparked a major integrity crisis for Cricket Australia. However, only captain Steve Smith and batsmen David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, who was caught with the sandpaper in his pocket, were banned for their part in the scandal. In a video posted on Instagram, Khawaja, who released the excerpt of his autobiography on Saturday, said he had wanted to "come clean" about the incident since 2018.

"I haven't thrown anyone under the bus," added the 39-year-old, who retired from international cricket in January. "The guys that are currently in the team right now and the other people that were there on the South African tour, including me, we're not the victims. "These three guys (Bancroft, Warner and Smith) took the blame for all of us, and they're the victims." Khawaja said he had spoken with the three players involved in "Sandpapergate", and that he had promised Warner he would share his side of the story. "These three guys deserve justice. And I haven't pointed fingers at anyone," he added. "I'm still searching for what I was searching all those years ago for us — me included — to take the blame together as a team so we can all move on from this once and for all." Australia's test side returned to South Africa for the first time since 2018 last month and were beaten 2-1 by the hosts in the three-match series, which was overshadowed in part by discussions of the scandal and the upcoming release of Khawaja's book.

EDINBURGH, Nov 8 : The New Zealand pair of Jordie Barrett and Will Jordan could miss next weekend's Nations Championship clash with Wales, after they picked up injuries at Murrayfield against Scotland on Saturday. Jordan suffered a suspected hamstring injury in the second half of the All Blacks’ convincing 43-21 victory, while Barrett was taken off for a head injury assessment (HIA) which he failed. He had a clash with Scotland substitute Blair Kinghorn. "Jordie failed his HIA, so it’s not sure whether he’ll be available this week, but we’ll get a bit of clarity later,” the All Blacks coach Dave Rennie said. On Jordan, who is the All Blacks’ leading all-time try-scorer, the coach added: “He might have tweaked a hamstring. We’ll assess that, and I’m not sure of the severity of it.”

New Zealand are already without several key players, including inspirational loose forward Ardie Savea, for their four-match November programme in Britain, but had little problem shrugging off the Scottish challenge, even though their hosts were within three points at halftime. “It was an ill-disciplined first half with a couple of yellow cards,” said Rennie of his team, who had both Wallace Sititi and Peter Lakai sent to the sin-bin. “You give Scotland opportunities near finish zone, they're going to hit you, but we were better in the second half.  “We went to a contestable kick game to limit their time from a counterattack point of view, and were a lot more clinical, and we dominated territory a bit better. “You just saw us lose our shape a couple of times, and from turnover we had two or three really gilt-edge opportunities that we spilt,” added the coach. The All Blacks play against Wales in Cardiff on Saturday.

PARIS, Nov 8 : France's Tom Laperche clinched victory in the Route du Rhum's Ultim class in his first appearance, mastering a transatlantic race that knocked out three rival boats. The 29-year-old skipper crossed the finish line in Pointe-a-Pitre at 10:31 p.m. on Saturday (0231 GMT on Sunday) aboard SVR-Lazartigue, completing the 3,542-nautical-mile race from Saint-Malo to Guadeloupe in 6 days, 13 hours, 27 minutes and 40 seconds. He set a race record, beating Charles Caudrelier's 2022 mark of 6 days, 19 hours, 47 minutes and 25 seconds. "I've always seen incredible images of finishes here, of great champions over the decades," Laperche said after his victory.

"My dream, first of all, was to one day sail these boats, perhaps to do some solo sailing, and why not race the Route du Rhum? So to win it at the helm of the most beautiful of the boats in the 2026 edition makes me very, very happy." Laperche, who won the Fastnet Race and the Transat Cafe L'Or last year, was locked in an intense battle with Armel Le Cleac'h in the early part of the race. But the skipper of Maxi Banque Populaire XI eventually capsized off the Azores on Wednesday morning, three days after the start. Le Cleac'h, winner of the 2016-17 Vendee Globe, was rescued by a Panamanian cargo ship. He was not the only one to abandon in the Ultim class, whose trimarans are 32 metres long and 23 metres wide (105 feet by 75 feet). Defending champion Charles Caudrelier was forced out on Tuesday due to foil damage on his new Maxi Edmond de Rothschild — Gitana 18. Anthony Marchand, skipper of Actual Ultim 4, also dropped out of the transatlantic race on Wednesday, two days after suffering a major technical problem with his central rudder. The retirements left the way clear for Laperche, one of the most talented skippers of his generation, who has been mentored by 2012-13 Vendee Globe winner François Gabart. The Ultims were the first boats to finish. The IMOCAs — 60-foot (18-metre) monohulls used in the Vendee Globe and the Ocean Race — are expected to reach Guadeloupe on Tuesday, with MACSF skipper Corentin Horeau leading the fleet.

Source: Reuters
